text:
Mia: Heads-up — over the last 10 days we've seen a 34% increase in requests that go beyond our 8k token threshold. Not huge qps but heavy tail on context length. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sam: Do you have a breakdown by region and streaming vs non-streaming?
Mia: Quick paste from the sampling job (rolling 24h):
```
# qps by context bucket
<=2048: 420 qps
2049-8192: 88 qps
>8192: 26 qps
# streaming vs non-streaming for >8192
streaming: 18 qps
non-streaming: 8 qps
```
Mia: Region split for the >8192 bucket: US-west 62%, EU 28%, APAC 10%
Jules: Oof — long contexts are all in US-west. That explains the local GPU pressure we've been seeing during PST peak.
Ahmed: Any change in average tokens-per-request? that affects KV cache hit-rate and batching efficiency.
Mia: Avg tokens/request for >8192 grew from 9.1k -> 12.4k over 2 weeks. KV cache eviction rate up ~14%.
Rachel: We also hit a soft network egress cap on one US-west subnet yesterday, autoscaler retried pods and latency spiked briefly. ops-bot posted alerts. :eyes:
ops-bot: autoscaler: scale-up triggered for gw-inference-pool-west (added 4 g4dn-equivalents) at 2026-02-28T19:42:06Z
Sam: Cost note: those extra preemptible instances + streaming throughput means GPU hours/day up ~22%. Need estimates for monthly commit impact if trends persist.
Jules: Propose short-term smoothing: 1) move 20% of >8k streaming traffic to dedicated streaming clusters with longer-lived KV layers, 2) cap per-request sequence length at 40k tokens for hosted tier (soft fail + suggestion to use dedicated).
Ahmed: For (1) we need to verify model shard/quant config is compatible. Also network bandwidth for long-KV warm starts — we should prebake prefix caches for top 200 callers.
Mia: I ran a quick sim — moving 20% to dedicated streaming pool reduces peak GPU hours by ~9% and reduces KV eviction by ~6%.
Rachel: Region constraint: EU-dedicated capacity is limited next two weeks (vendor maintenance). If we shift EU traffic to dedicated, we'll need fallback to US which increases egress/cost.
Sam: Can we do a cheap mitigation: enable aggressive prefix caching + lower batch sizes for >8k in hosted until dedicated pool ready? That should control latency without big infra changes.
Jules: Aggressive prefix caching helps, but it increases memory pressure on nodes; might force us to increase reserved memory per pod which lowers packing density. Trade-offs.
Mia: Suggested immediate plan (next 72h):
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for >8k requests in US-west only (monitor memory + eviction)
- Create a 8xGPU dedicated streaming pool (us-west) on on-demand class for hot callers (20% traffic)
- Add a soft length limit to hosted (warn + link to docs)
- Ops: watchlist for egress alerts in us-west subnet
Sam: Action owners?
Mia: I'll own cache toggle and the soft limit rollout.
Jules: I'll scope the dedicated pool config (shard + quantization) and estimate cost delta.
Ahmed: I'll prep the prefix prebake job and a small canary for network warming.
Rachel: I'll open a ticket with cloud infra about egress headroom in US-west and request temporary bump if needed.
ops-bot: ticket CREATED: #INC-2026-gw-egress-bump by Rachel at 2026-02-28T20:01:12Z
Sam: Thanks — please post short daily updates in this thread. If cost delta >15% monthly, we'll bring to finance for reserve re-eval. :+1:
Mia: Will do. First brief update tomorrow 09:30 PST.
Jules: One more thought — medium-term (2-4 weeks) we should evaluate a model-split: a streaming-optimized quantized variant (lower mem, better KV behavior) vs a short-context high-throughput variant. That could cut GPU hours by ~12% for the long-tail.
Ahmed: +1. I'll prototype perf numbers with our 30k-token eval set.
Mia: Cool. Tagging follow-ups: @Sam @Jules @Ahmed @Rachel.
Sam: 👍
Rachel: :eyes: keeping an eye on egress
Mia: Closing for now — let's reconvene after the canary results.
